create.name: Stephen Gray
create.bio:
Stephen Gray is a writer, podcaster and ceremony leader who has spent about fifty years combining contemplative practice with the use of sacred plants. He studied Tibetan Buddhism for more than two decades and occasionally taught within it, took part for around twelve years in Native American Church peyote ceremonies, and has been a guest member of the Santo Daime church, which uses ayahuasca as its sacrament. For a decade he helped run Vancouver's Spirit Plant Medicine Conference in Canada.

He writes and speaks about how entheogens might be approached with care, preparation and respect for the traditions they come from, as one support for spiritual awakening alongside meditation and prayer. His books include Returning to Sacred World, a guide to spiritual practice in a time of upheaval, and two collections he edited and contributed to: Cannabis and Spirituality and How Psychedelics Can Help Save the World. A further book on plant spirit teachings is due in 2027. On his StephenGray Vision podcast he holds long conversations with researchers, elders and guides in the psychedelic field, and he leads cannabis meditation and sound-journey ceremonies.

videos.title: For the Beauty and the Wisdom: A Sacred Slideshow

books.title: Returning to Sacred World: A Spiritual Toolkit for the Emerging Reality
books.author: Stephen Gray
books.description: Gray's own guide to spiritual practice at a time of social and ecological change. He draws on Buddhist meditation, prayer and indigenous plant-medicine traditions to suggest ways of waking up to our connection with each other and the Earth.

books.title: Cannabis and Spirituality: An Explorer's Guide to an Ancient Plant Spirit Ally
books.author: Stephen Gray
books.description: A collection edited by Gray, with chapters from eighteen writers, on using cannabis with intention in meditation, yoga, chanting, ceremony and creative work. He also contributes chapters of his own.

books.title: How Psychedelics Can Help Save the World: Visionary and Indigenous Voices Speak Out
books.author: Stephen Gray
books.description: An anthology edited by Gray in which scientists, indigenous elders and practitioners consider what entheogens might offer at a time of planetary crisis. Contributors include Christopher Bache and Dennis McKenna.

Content: his work centres on psychedelics and entheogens (ayahuasca, peyote, psilocybin, cannabis, and in his podcast also MDMA, LSD and coca). Nothing condition-led was kept, but some podcast titles are condition-led ('Psychedelics for Trauma and Addiction'); the channel as a whole is interviews on plant medicine and spirituality. Please check it fits.

Thin and borderline 'teacher': no current classes, courses or events (his events page shows none since April 2023); the listing rests on 3 books and 2 videos. He says he leads cannabis meditation and sound-journey ceremonies, but none is listed.

Most of his YouTube channel is his podcast, where he interviews others; only the two kept videos have him as the main voice. 'For the Beauty and the Wisdom: A Sacred Slideshow' was checked by title and length only.

Books confirmed on Open Library: https://openlibrary.org/isbn/1846943906 (Returning to Sacred World, O Books/John Hunt 2010), https://openlibrary.org/isbn/1620555832 (Cannabis and Spirituality, Park Street Press) and https://openlibrary.org/isbn/1644114917 (How Psychedelics Can Help Save the World, Inner Traditions 2022).
